name: LTX 2.5 IC-LoRA — video to video (pose control + audio)
description:
Make a new character perform the movements of the people in your video. Upload a source video with people in it (and, optionally, a start image): the body, hand and face poses of every frame are detected (DWPose) and drawn as a stick-figure guide, so LTX 2.5 generates a new video in which the characters move like the original — while their look, the setting and the lighting come from your prompt and start image. A freshly generated soundtrack is added (the original audio is not kept).

Only the poses carry over — not the background, clothes or camera look — so this gives far more freedom than the depth or canny versions. The source needs clearly visible people; a clip with nobody in it gives the model no guide at all.

The start image becomes the opening frame; a still of your new character in the first frame's pose works best. Untick "Use a start image" to let the prompt alone set the look — then no image is needed. "Enhance prompt with AI" lets a small Gemma model rewrite your prompt into a fuller description first. Lower "Control strength" to let the movements drift further from the source.

Only the start of your clip is used ("Clip length used", default 5 s), at its own frame rate and aspect ratio. The video is rendered in two passes, a fast 8-step pass at the working resolution and then a 2× upscale pass, so a working resolution of 512 gives a 1024p result. Clip length and resolution drive the time.

promptGuides.label: LTX union control (depth / canny / pose) — Lightricks
promptGuides.tip: Describe the look you want — style, materials, characters, lighting, sound — not the motion or the control map: the movement comes from your video.

author: Lightricks (ComfyUI-LTXVideo)

exposedParameters.label: Source video (the people whose movements to copy)
Prompt (scene / style / action / sound)
exposedParameters.default: A shiny chrome robot dancing on a neon-lit city rooftop at night, reflections sliding over its metal body, light rain, cinematic lighting. Upbeat electronic music.

exposedParameters.label: Control strength (how strictly the source's movements are followed)
Working resolution (short side, multiple of 64 — the final video is 2× this)
Clip length used (seconds, max 10 — only the start of your video is processed)
